result: Desktop now classifies generated ProjectionLifecycleEvent DTOs against the exact frozen Workstream authority, cursor namespace, projection/layout watermarks, and the Core-owned invalidation event allowlist before scheduling a refresh. Valid events coalesce into one serialized bounded projectionController.refresh call; routine draft/Pi events, foreign or malformed authority, stale cursor/revision, missing authority, and unsupported capability/event input fail closed without refreshing or remounting the Canvas shell.

presentation_contract.surface_kind: Focusa Desktop Mission Canvas Svelte GUI tab
continuity_invariants: generated event and projection DTOs remain transport-owned
refresh is bounded and does not remount the shell

generated_transport.projection_refresh: MissionCanvasProjectionController.refresh delegates to the generated projectionGet boundary
generated_transport.ownership: Generated operation registry, OpenAPI, TypeScript client, DTOs, and validators remain transport owners; Desktop adds only scoped event classification and bounded refresh scheduling.

implementation: event.classify validates generated ProjectionLifecycleEvent and WorkstreamAuthorityContext DTOs, compares the complete authority chain, checks the generated event-kind relevance set, and rejects stale or mismatched cursors and watermarks.

invalidation.coalesce accepts only events classified as projection-invalidating, deduplicates queued event IDs/cursors, and schedules one refresh window without local contribution eligibility or layout resolution.
Refreshes are serialized; events arriving while projectionController.refresh is in flight remain pending for a subsequent bounded refresh, and disposed controllers cannot refresh after scope cleanup.
Runtime supplies the exact bound authority and projection durable cursor and invokes projectionController.refresh; routine Pi/draft events do not cause a whole-projection refresh.
Empty/ineligible contribution events can request a canonical projection reread, but Desktop never invents a contribution, panel, layout node, or replacement content.

negative_cases.foreign_workstream: A foreign Workstream or foreign nested Attachment authority is rejected by event.classify; no refresh is queued.
negative_cases.missing_authority: A coalescer call without an exact authority context returns false and cannot invoke the refresh callback.
negative_cases.stale_cursor: Equal/regressed cursors and cursor namespace mismatches are rejected before event relevance or refresh scheduling.
negative_cases.stale_revision: Projection or layout revision regressions are rejected; current projection state remains the refresh source.
negative_cases.unavailable_capability_or_unsupported_ev: Malformed/unknown generated event input and routine event kinds are ignored; capability resolution remains Core-owned and no client-local capability inference occurs.
negative_cases.ineligible_or_empty_contribution: A valid contribution_omitted event may trigger a Core projection reread only when its cursor/watermark advances; no local contribution or layout is synthesized.
negative_cases.refresh_burst: Multiple valid events in one window cause one callback; duplicate IDs and non-advancing queued cursors do not add work.
negative_cases.refresh_overlap: Events received during an in-flight refresh are retained and run after the first refresh completes; refreshes never overlap.
negative_cases.dispose: Disposal cancels pending timers and prevents callbacks from a disposed controller.
